title: Extraction of adsorptive high-purity silica from high-iron, high-calcium fly ash with a low alumina-to-silica ratio
content: High-iron, high-calcium fly ash (HICFA) with a low alumina–silica ratio is produced massively by coal-fired thermal power plants around the world. The properties and behaviors of HICFA during element extraction processes are quite different from those of the extensively studied high-alumina fly ash. In this study, a novel and targeted method for the extraction of silica from HICFA was developed. Through a series of combined acid–alkali extraction steps, high-quality silica with high purity (99.53%) and specific surface area (738 m2 g−1), as well as medium-purity silica with a high specific surface area, was obtained from HICFA. Both types of silica exhibit adsorption capacities for organic dyes. Easy access to the raw materials, low energy consumption, and a high silicon extraction rate (98.07%) make this a feasible strategy for the resource utilization of HICFAs.
